body.title: [front] Mention helpers take the AgentResource
body.body:
## Description

`resolveModel`, `resolveModelForMentionedAgent`, `isAgentRestrictedBySpaceUsage` and `canAgentBeUsedInProjectConversation` take an `AgentResource` instead of a `LightAgentConfigurationType`. Message post and edit pass the mentioned agent's resource and serialize it only for the agent message they create. Callers that only held a serialized configuration (retry, final status and handover promotion, the agent loop's stream fallback) resolve the message's pinned version with `fetchByIdsAndVersions` (fetch check skipped, as before); the trigger-limit message takes the trigger's resource. The similar-agents check and the tag-suggestion route build their LLM prompts from `AgentResource`s (`batchFetchInstructions` for the instructions) instead of serializing every agent; the tag-suggestion response now returns the `{ sId, name }` its type declares instead of full configurations.

## Tests

New tests: the similar-agents prompt carries the instructions, and the tag-suggestion route describes the agents and returns `{ sId, name }`. Tests build resources instead of fake configurations (`permissions.test.ts` creates agents with the requested spaces). 937 tests across conversation, models, triggers and sandbox pass; the only failures are `sandbox/.../grep_files.test.ts`, unchanged and failing locally on its own. Typecheck clean.

## Risk

Low to medium: retry and final-status updates now read the pinned agent version (one query by id and version) instead of the message's serialized configuration.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy front.

body.title: [front] Add architecture guidance to the build agents and skills skill
body.body:
## Description

The "Build Agents and Skills" skill helps users write agents but never pushes back on over-built setups: expensive models, long prompts, too many tools or sub-agents. A new `<architecture_guidance>` section (shared in `agent_suggestions_shared.ts`) tells the builder to pick the leanest structure (one agent, then agent + skills, then a sub-agent only when a part needs its own model, tools or isolation), default to Auto Fast, suggest compact instructions and minimize tool calls.


## Tests

* Conversational building evals pass locally, including two new architecture scenarios added in the stacked eval PR.

## Risk

Medium. Prompt only, but the skill is no longer flagged so every workspace gets it; worst case the builder recommends a cheaper model too eagerly or declines a sub-agent the user really needed. Revert to roll back.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy `front`. No migration, no flag.

body.title: Draft: durable per-case Temporal eval backend
body.body:
## Description

Draft backend for launching Henry's evals remotely, rather than keeping the evaluator alive on a laptop or Computer session. This implements per-case/stage Temporal orchestration, not a wrapper retrying the entire CLI.

- Dedicated `evals` worker / `evals-v1` queue, parent run + bounded child case workflows, and separately persisted agent/judge stages.
- Workspace-scoped Postgres run and step records, additive migration, input hash, conversation/message IDs, answers and scores.
- Authenticated `/api/v1/w/{wId}/evals/runs` launch/list/status/detail/cancel endpoints. Flag-gated admin-only pilot; launching uses a server-side, unscoped admin API key re-authorized at execution time.
- Retry-safe run submission with a caller UUID and Temporal duplicate rejection. Stage launch claims plus **no automatic retries of ambiguous conversation creation/posting**; ambiguity is a visible failure requiring inspection, not an exactly-once claim.
- Extract the dependency-free scoring core from `x/henry/dust-evals`; the existing CLI re-exports it so rubric / voting behavior stays shared.
- No Frame in the repo: the collaborative UI should be authored separately in the Computer and published into a Pod.

### Draft boundaries / must resolve before enabling

See `front/lib/evals/README.md` for the API contract and detailed rollout gates.

- Provision the hosted worker separately. Nothing in this PR deploys or starts evals.
- Real Temporal/Postgres fault-injection and CI validation are still required.
- Wire retention, workspace deletion/scrub and relocation for the new records before enablement.
- Cancellation only stops *new stages*. In-flight Dust conversations can keep running (including after a deadline).
- Ambiguous launch requires inspection; idempotent conversation/message creation is a follow-up.
- No hard per-run credit budget or workspace-wide run quota yet. Existing programmatic gates and bounded fanout are not a spend guarantee.
- `ownCostCredits` deliberately excludes sub-agents and may not yet be final accounting.
- Inputs are frozen, but agent instructions/tools/knowledge are not version-pinned. No reproducibility claim yet.
- Admin-only result access. Pod-specific permissions, annotations, selective reruns and the Frame are follow-ups.

## Tests

Local shallow clone, edits and `git status` / `git diff` reviewed in the Computer; rebased on current main before preparing the push.

Passed locally:
- `bun test x/henry/dust-evals/src/grading.test.ts x/henry/dust-evals/src/model-selection.test.ts`: **33 tests**.
- **7 portable smoke checks** using Bun: 2 case-planning checks with a temporary Vitest-to-Bun import adapter, and 5 temporary mocked workflow checks for stage order, repeated polling, ambiguous launch, cancellation and bounded child concurrency. These are not real Temporal integration tests.
- Bun syntax-only transpilation of all changed TypeScript sources.
- `oxlint` on changed TypeScript files: zero warnings/errors (not a substitute for repository Biome checks).
- `git diff --check`.

Added repository Vitest coverage for input limits, case planning, orchestration, persistence/idempotency and workspace access isolation. Those Vitest suites, full typechecking, repository formatting, migrations, worker bundles and live integration were **not run locally** because the repository dependencies/services are not installed. Validation is delegated to PR CI and a provisioned integration environment. Do not merge/enable based only on the portable checks.

## Risk

**High if enabled before follow-up validation; disabled by default.** New execution path can incur API/model/tool spend. Workspace-scoped rows contain prompts and answers, so retention and authorization need review. Conversation side effects are not transactional with eval checkpoints; failure semantics deliberately prefer a visible uncertain launch over duplicate spend.

The scoring move is shared with the existing CLI and should be covered by its unchanged grading tests. Review CLI standalone-checkout/build assumptions after the extraction. Confirm the proposed feature-flag owner and infrastructure ownership.

No credentials, production evaluation data, generated reports, or local test harnesses are committed.

## Deploy Plan

1. Keep `durable_evals` disabled. Complete CI, migration/schema review, retention/deletion integration, and fault-injection testing.
2. Apply the additive pre-deploy migration.
3. Deploy front API and provision the dedicated `evals` worker using existing worker-image conventions; verify the `evals-v1` queue and front namespace.
4. Only after review, enable for an internal test workspace with a capped dedicated API key and a tiny read-only dataset.
5. Build/publish the Frame separately, with server-side viewer authorization. No browser-exposed API keys.

Rollback: disable the flag, handle any already-running Dust conversations separately, then drain/stop the worker. Retain the additive tables until cleanup is agreed. **No deployment or production eval run was performed while authoring this draft.**

body.title: security: restrict Freshservice OAuth token endpoint to Freshworks domains
body.body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: `parse_freshworks_org_url` validated domain *format* (RFC-compliant hostname regex) but not *destination*. Any syntactically valid domain — including `attacker.com` — was accepted and would receive Dust's platform-wide Freshworks OAuth client credentials (`OAUTH_FRESHWORKS_CLIENT_ID` / `OAUTH_FRESHWORKS_CLIENT_SECRET`) in a `Basic` auth header. A workspace member with no special role could trigger this via the setup/finalize OAuth routes.
- **Fix**: Add `FRESHWORKS_ALLOWED_DOMAIN_SUFFIXES = [".myfreshworks.com", ".freshworks.com"]` checked after the regex. The leading-dot prefix correctly closes two bypass patterns: bare parent domains (`myfreshworks.com`) and suffix-injection names (`evil.myfreshworks.com.attacker.com`).
- **Behavior change**: The previous code intentionally accepted "custom organization domains" (comment: `// including custom domains`). This PR removes that: only `*.myfreshworks.com` and `*.freshworks.com` are now valid endpoints. Any existing Freshservice connector configured with a non-Freshworks custom domain will fail on the next `refresh()` call. Prod should be checked for such connections before deploy.

## Risk

Low for new connections; moderate for any existing connections with custom Freshworks domains. The allowlist covers the documented Freshworks OAuth hostname patterns. Rollback is a one-line revert to the format-only check.

## Testing plan

- [x] 5 unit tests pass: `accepts_standard_myfreshworks_domain`, `accepts_freshworks_subdomain`, `strips_scheme_and_trailing_slash`, `rejects_ips_paths_ports_and_bare_hosts`, `rejects_non_freshworks_domains` (includes bare-domain and suffix-injection cases)
- [ ] Confirm no prod Freshservice connectors are configured with non-Freshworks custom domains before deploying

body.title: [front] Price consumption attribution at the run usage's inference region
body.body:
## Description

Closes https://github.com/dust-tt/tasks/issues/10742

Consumption attribution derived token rates at global pricing, even for runs served from an EU endpoint. EU messages therefore under-attributed gross credits by the 10% regional uplift, and the reconciled input row absorbed the gap.

Concrete example:
- Attribution cache-naive cost at global rates: `15,901 × $10/M + 320 × $50/M = 175,010` µUSD, matching the debug script's `cacheNaiveCostMicroUsd`.
- Recorded provider cost at EU rates with cache write: `15,901 × 11 + 15,898 × (13.75 − 11) + 320 × 55 = 236,231` µUSD, matching exactly.
- The input row was reconciled ~39% above its gross: 10% from the missing EU uplift, ~25% from the cache-write premium (expected, attribution is cache-naive), ~1% from bill rounding.

Changes:
- `RunUsageForAttribution` now includes `region`; `getRunTokenRates` passes `inferenceRegion` (via `inferenceRegionForEndpointRegion`, `null` → global) to `computeTokensCostForUsageInMicroUsd`.
- Bumps `AGENT_MESSAGE_CONSUMPTION_ATTRIBUTION_VERSION` to 10
- New `@cc rates-match-recorded-cost-pricing` contract on `getRunTokenRates`.
- `debug_agent_message_tool_footprints.ts` uses the region for its cache-naive figures too, so EU runs no longer show negative cache savings.

Known gap, out of scope: the batch path (`RunResource.recordRunUsage`) stores `region: null` even though `costMicroUsd` is priced at the endpoint's region, so EU batch rows don't record where inference ran. This doesn't affect attribution: batch runs only come from reinforcement analysis and are never part of an agent message's `runIds`.

## Tests

- New unit test: EU rows are 1.1× global for every attributed row, and a `null` region prices as global.
- `agent_message_consumption_attribution` suite passes (157 tests).

## Risk

Low. Only changes attribution rows for EU runs on models with a regional uplift; billing is unaffected.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy `front`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body.title: security: bind remote-database credentials to their workspace
body.body:
## Summary
- Snowflake MCP key-pair login refuses `authInfo.extra.credentialId` unless the oauth credential belongs to the caller's workspace and its content is a Snowflake key-pair. The client is not constructed otherwise.
- Snowflake and BigQuery connector create/update refuse a credential whose `metadata.workspace_id` or `provider` does not match the connector, before the connection is tested or `connectionId` is saved. Sync and permission reads apply the same check.
- Public table upsert rejects `remote_database_table_id` and `remote_database_secret_id` from non-system callers. System keys can set them only after the credential is fetched and accepted as a Snowflake or BigQuery secret for that workspace.

Tables already stored in core keep their current secret id until the next successful upsert. A connector whose saved credential fails this check stops syncing until it is rebound to a credential for its own workspace.

## Test plan
- [x] `front` credential helper and Snowflake tool tests
- [x] Public table upsert tests: non-system rejection, cross-workspace system-key rejection, matching system-key upsert
- [x] Connector `getCredentials` / `getConnectorAndCredentials` tests
- [x] `tsgo --noEmit` in `front`, `front-api`, and `connectors`
- [ ] Confirm an existing Snowflake or BigQuery connector still syncs after deploy

body.title: security: enforce credential/connection ownership on connector and webhook binding
body.body:
## Summary

Three IDOR vulnerabilities (B04) that allow a workspace admin to bind a foreign OAuth credential or connection to their own connector or webhook source:

- **Notion/Slack private-integration config** (`privateIntegrationCredentialId`): `POST /api/w/:wId/data_sources/:dsId/managed/config/privateIntegrationCredentialId` forwarded the caller-supplied credential ID verbatim to connectors with no ownership check. Added `checkCredentialOwnership` — rejects any `cred_` ID whose `metadata.workspace_id` differs from the caller's workspace (403).

- **Connector re-authorization** (`managed/update connectionId`): `POST /api/w/:wId/data_sources/:dsId/managed/update` accepted a foreign `connectionId` and passed it to `connectorsAPI.updateConnector` unchecked. Added `checkConnectionOwnership` — rejects any `con_` ID whose `metadata.user_id` or `workspace_id` doesn't match the caller (403).

- **Webhook source create/rebind** (`webhook_sources` POST + PATCH): Both routes forwarded a caller-supplied `connectionId`/`oauthConnectionId` to `createWebhooks` or stored it without user ownership check. Added `checkConnectionOwnership` on both paths (403).

## Testing
Added new tests

## Risk

Low — changes are additive guards that fire only when the ID's metadata workspace/user doesn't match the caller. Legitimate same-workspace bindings are unaffected. The 403 response is the same shape used elsewhere in these routes.

## Deploy
1. Deploy front

body.title: [extension] fix: compile Lingui macros and provide i18n in the extension

labels.name: package-chrome-extension-preview
labels.description: Package a production chrome extension

body.body: ## Description Shared `front` components now import Lingui macros: `InAppBanner` since #33771, and more as we translate the product UI. The extension bundles those components, but it is built with `ts-loader` only, so the macros were never compiled: - `@lingui/react/macro` resolved to its uncompiled module, which **throws on evaluation**. Since #33771, the chrome and firefox bundles crash at startup and the panel stays blank. `InAppBanner` is statically imported through `SidebarMenu` → `ConversationLayout` → `MainPage`, so `hideInAppBanner` doesn't prevent it. - With no `I18nProvider`, `useLingui()` and `` would also fail once compiled. This PR: - Adds `extension/config/webpack_lingui.ts`. The Lingui macro Babel plugin runs before `ts-loader` on `.ts`/`.tsx`, parsing TypeScript only, so `ts-loader` still strips the types. `.po` catalogs are loaded with `@lingui/loader`. Both are used by the chrome, firefox and front webpack configs. - Wraps each platform app root (`ChromeApp`, `FirefoxApp`, `FrontApp`) in an `I18nProvider` with the `i18n` instance from `@app/lib/i18n/i18n`. The extension keeps rendering en-US. - Includes `front/lib/i18n/po.d.ts` in the extension `tsconfig` so `tsgo` resolves the catalog imports. - Adds `extension/CONTRACTS` (`lingui-macros-compiled`, `app-root-provides-i18n`) and updates the `dust-i18n` skill. ## Tests - Built chrome and firefox in production mode, then loaded each `main.html` in jsdom with stubbed `chrome`/`browser` APIs. - Before: `Uncaught Error: The macro you imported from "@lingui/react/macro" is being executed outside the context of compilation`, and nothing renders. - After: the app renders; the only error is the login redirect, which jsdom can't follow. The bundle contains no macro module. - Rendered a temporary probe component (not committed) at the chrome root, with its messages extracted into the en-US catalog. It used `` with markup, `t` with a placeholder, `msg` and `plural`, and rendered `Hello Ada, welcome.|Probe label|3 agents|Try it`. - `npm run tsgo` in `extension` passes. - Not tested in a real browser yet: adding `package-chrome-extension-preview` to get a preview package. ## Risk - **Bundle output:** chrome and firefox builds now go through Babel. The emitted code is unchanged apart from the compiled macros. - **Build time:** chrome production builds take about 30s instead of 20s. - **Front platform:** its build already fails on `main` (`front/types/mount_path.ts` imports Node's `path`). This PR doesn't change that. ## Deploy Plan Release a new extension version. Nothing to deploy on the web app side. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body.title: security(connectors): use repository.owner.login in GitHub PR webhook handler
body.body:
## Summary

The `pull_request` webhook handler in the GitHub connector was deriving the repository owner login from `sender.login` (the user who triggered the event) when the payload did not carry an `organization` field. `sender` is the PR merger, not the repository owner. An attacker who controls a GitHub login matching an org name could cause the connector to sync code from a namesake repository they control instead of the victim's.

- **Root cause**: `isPullRequestPayload` accepted a discriminated union of `{ organization }` | `{ sender }` and the handler used `organization.login ?? sender.login`.
- **Fix**: Add `owner: UserSchema` to `RepositorySchema` (always present in every GitHub webhook payload). Change the handler to read `repository.owner.login` unconditionally. Simplify `PullRequestPayloadSchema` by removing the `organization | sender` union — it is no longer needed for ownership resolution.
- **Contract**: Added `@cc pr-owner-from-repository` to `isPullRequestPayload` documenting that `repository.owner.login` MUST be used.

**Follow-ups (not blocking):**
- `issue` and `discussion` handlers use the same `org ?? user.login` pattern; `user.login` is the event actor, not necessarily the repo owner. Should be aligned in a follow-up.
- Full file migration from io-ts to zod per `use-zod-for-runtime-validation` contract — deferred since migrating one schema in isolation would leave a mixed file.

## Testing
Connector webhook path — no automated tests for this handler. Verified via TypeScript typecheck pass and payload schema validation.

## Risk
Low rollout risk: `repository.owner` is always present in GitHub webhook payloads per the GitHub API spec. The schema change (removing `organization | sender` union) only loosens the validation — previously valid payloads remain valid.

body.title: security(front): remove upsertArgs spread allowing content injection and cross-datasource writes
body.body:
## Summary

`upsertDocumentToDatasource` and `upsertSectionDocumentToDatasource` spread caller-supplied `upsertArgs` via `...restArgs` / `...upsertArgs` **after** every explicitly set field in the `upsertDocument` call — including `text` and `dataSource`. Since `POST /api/w/:wId/data_sources/:dsId/files` parses the body as raw JSON with no runtime schema validation, a caller could inject any key and silently override a server-resolved field.

**Fix**: Remove the open-ended spreads in document functions and replace with explicit field extraction (`document_id`, `title`, `parent_id`, `parents`). Also adds `parent_id` and `parents` to the `Pick` type (used by callers but previously undeclared). Adds `@cc upsert-args-no-server-override` contract scoping which fields document functions may pass through.

**Not changed**: `upsertTableToDatasource` and `upsertExcelToDatasource` still spread `...restArgs` — `UpsertTableArgs` excludes `dataSource` and `auth`, and Excel processing depends on the spread for worksheet-specific fields.

## Testing
- `npx tsgo --noEmit` passes
- Biome lint passes
- Verified all callers: `MultipleFilesUpload.tsx` passes only `{ title, document_id }`; `TableUploadOrEditModal.tsx` passes only table args — no existing call site is affected

## Risk
Low. Conservative change: removes a broad spread and replaces it with explicit extraction matching the declared interface.

## Deploy
1. Deploy front

body.title: [front] feat: add disable_frames_v2 flag to opt a workspace out of Frames v2

labels.name: sdk-ack
labels.description: Used to acknowledge that you are not breaking the public API.

labels.name: sse-ack
labels.description: Used to acknowledge that this a front-sse deploy is required.

body.body:
## Problem

Frames v2 is rolled out globally at 100% (`global_feature_flags.frames_v2`, since 2026-09-28). Under Frames v2, the `interactive_content` MCP server only registers `export_interactive_content_file` (`frames-v2-tool-allowlist`), so `create_interactive_content_file` is gone, including its `template` mode: server-side instantiation of a Frame from a knowledge-base document, without the model reading or regenerating the source.

Frames v2 has no equivalent. `dsbx frame` only offers `publish`, `call` and `share-link`, and the sandbox mount only exposes conversation and Pod files, so a template stored in a data source cannot even be copied into a Frame folder.

Customer's proposal agent is built around template mode ("uses only the approved V15 knowledge and Frame template", no reading or recreating it). Since Frames v2 reached them, it fails with `MCP error -32602: Tool create_interactive_content_file not found` and posts a blocker instead of the proposal.

## Fix

Add a `disable_frames_v2` workspace flag that makes the workspace behave as if `frames_v2` were off:

- `applyFeatureFlagOverrides` drops `frames_v2` from the effective flags when `disable_frames_v2` is present, whether `frames_v2` comes from the global rollout or a workspace flag.
- It is applied in `getFeatureFlagsForWorkspace`, which every flag read goes through (`hasFeatureFlag`, `withFeatureFlag`, the front-end `/feature-flags` endpoint), so all `frames_v2` checks honour it without call-site changes.
- `disable_frames_v2` is added to the SDK's flag names.

## Caveat

`frames_v2` also gates viewing: Frames v2 Frames render as unsupported content and the `/frames` routes refuse them while the opt-out is on. Customer has 19 Frames v2 Frames, all created on 2026-10-01, which will stop rendering until the opt-out is removed. The flag is `ask_owner` for that reason.

## Tests

`lib/auth.global_feature_flags.test.ts`: the opt-out overrides the global rollout and a workspace `frames_v2` flag, and leaves other flags untouched. Both new tests fail without the override.

body.title: Ungate Pod egress & env-var admin and request_egress_domain from the Frames functions flags
body.body:
## Description

Pod network (egress) and environment settings are Computer platform features. They were originally built alongside Pod Functions and shipped behind the `sandbox_functions` flag as a dust-only rollout guard; when Pod Functions were removed in favor of Frames v2 (`31933`), the gates were carried over to `frames_v2` + `frames_v2_functions` (via `withSandboxFunctionInvocationFeature`) simply to keep that guard alive — not because the surfaces depend on Frames. They don't: egress allowlists and env vars apply to every Computer (conversation sandboxes included), regardless of whether Frame functions are in use. This ungates them to every workspace with the Computer enabled:

- **Workspace admin routes** (`/sandbox/*`, incl. egress-policy bulk/pods): drop the Frames gates; the parent sub-app keeps `ensureIsAdmin` only. Routes carry no feature-flag gate — `disable_computer_feature` is set on a single workspace and is slated for removal, so the Computer flag gates the UI only.
- **Pod settings routes** (`/spaces/:spaceId/sandbox/*`): drop the Frames gate with no flag gate replacing it; access control is per leaf (reads open to Pod readers, writes workspace-admin only). The now-unused `withComputerFeature` middleware is deleted.
- **UI**: `useComputerAdminAccess` loses `canAdministratePodNetwork` (its one consumer now uses `canAdministrateComputer`); `PodSettingsSection`'s Advanced-tab visibility and `PodSettingsAdvancedTab`'s sections gate on the Computer flag; `SandboxPage`'s now-constant network branch is simplified and the orphaned `NetworkSection` component is deleted.
- **`request_egress_domain` tool**: excluded only when the Computer is disabled. Its effective availability was already bounded by the Computer toolset; the Pod/workspace review surfaces it files into are ungated by this same stack, so the filing side and the approval side open together.

`withSandboxFunctionInvocationFeature` itself stays, and keeps gating what is genuinely Frame-functions territory: function invocation routes, frame databases, and the SSE invocation streams.

> [!NOTE]
> This is a rollout change: these surfaces become visible to **all workspaces with the Computer enabled** (the UI hides the Computer tab and the Pod Advanced tab behind the flag), not just Frames-flagged ones. The API routes themselves are not flag-gated at all — role and Pod-scope checks are the access control — so the one `disable_computer_feature` workspace could reach them directly until that flag is removed.

## Tests

Existing route/tool tests updated: the feature-flag 403 suites are removed along with the route gates (role/scope 403s and 404s remain covered), and `createSandboxTools` tests assert `request_egress_domain` ships without any Frames flags. Typecheck (front + front-api) and biome clean on all touched files.

## Risk

Worst case, a workspace sees Pod network/env-var settings earlier than intended — every surface stays admin-gated (or Pod-reader read-only where it already was) and agent requests remain admin-reviewed before granting anything. Safe to rollback (revert re-gates; any domain requests filed in the window simply remain pending).

## Deploy Plan

- [ ] Deploy front-api and front (no strict ordering; until both are out, the mismatch is only cosmetic — hidden sections or 403s on not-yet-ungated routes)

body.title: security: restrict Google Drive picker tokens to accessible Drive servers
body.body:
## Summary

`POST /api/w/:wId/google_drive/picker_token` accepted any `mcpServerId` and, when that server's first view was `platform_actions`, exchanged the admin workspace OAuth connection. `listByMCPServer` is only workspace-scoped, so a member could name a server they cannot access — including one that is not Google Drive — and receive the raw access token.

The route now:

- Rejects any id that is not an internal `google_drive` server in the caller's workspace with **400**, and does not call OAuth.
- Requires `read` or `admin` on at least one view of that server. Otherwise **404**, and no OAuth call. The system-space view does not authorize a normal member.
- Chooses `workspace` vs `personal` from those accessible views only.

Members who can use a shared Google Drive server still receive the picker token, including the workspace token when that server is configured for platform actions. `makeFileAuthorizationError` is only emitted by the Google Drive tools, so the in-product picker still sends a Drive server id.

## Testing

new unit tests

## Risk

Low. The legitimate picker path is unchanged. Requests that named another MCP server, or a Drive server the caller cannot access, now fail closed. Rollback is a revert of this commit.

## Deploy

1. Deploy front

body.title: [front] Add Figma remote MCP server behind a feature flag

labels.name: sdk-ack
labels.description: Used to acknowledge that you are not breaking the public API.

body.body:
## Description

Registers Figma's hosted MCP server (`https://mcp.figma.com/mcp`) as a default remote server, gated by the new dust-only `figma_mcp` feature flag. Figma only lets OAuth apps it has reviewed and approved connect to its MCP server and rejects dynamic client registration, so the preset uses static OAuth credentials with the `mcp:connect` scope. The connect dialog gets a Figma setup guide, like the Power BI and NetSuite ones, listing the three `/oauth/mcp_static/finalize` redirect URIs to register on the Figma app and the fixed authorization, token, resource and auth-method values to enter. Figma requires client credentials in a Basic header, which the guide calls out since the form defaults to `client_secret_post`.

Tool stakes and display labels cover the tool list from Figma's docs. Reads are `never_ask`, creates and uploads are `low`, and the general-purpose `use_figma` edit tool, shader and plugin source replacements, and Weave runs are `high`. The names have not yet been checked against a live `tools/list`, which needs an approved app; a mismatched key just falls back to prompting. The existing sparkle Figma logo was missing from the SDK and front icon lists, so it is wired through those and refreshed to the current brand-kit colors. The public integrations registry now skips remote presets gated behind a dust-only flag, so Figma stays off the marketing page until the flag graduates.

Dust's Figma OAuth app is still under Figma's review. The plan is to test and record the flow with the private app once it is approved, then swap to the public app in a follow-up, so this isn't currently testable E2E.

## Tests

Front tsgo and SDK tsc clean, biome clean. Vitest passes for the remote server configuration section, MCP server view resource, server metadata and feature flag suites. End-to-end OAuth against the private Figma app is pending Figma approval.

## Risk

Only workspaces with the `figma_mcp` flag can see the preset, and the flag is dust-only. Worst case, the Figma connection fails for the Dust workspace. Safe to rollback.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy front and the JS SDK types. Enable `figma_mcp` on the Dust workspace once Figma approves the app, connect, and verify the tool list matches the stakes before widening the flag.

body.title: Frame functions: name the egress-blocked domains on a failed invocation
body.body:
## Description

A Frame or Pod function whose `fetch()` hits a domain the egress allowlist blocks fails with a bare network error. The proxy writes the denial to the sandbox's deny log, but nothing reads that log for function sandboxes, so the agent has no way to learn which domain to declare. The Computer's bash tool already does this for the conversation sandbox: it reads the deny log after each command and appends the blocked domains to the tool output.

Stacked on the Frames v2 manifest `domains` PR (`31910`), which is stacked on the gate swap (`31909`).

**What this PR does:**

1. Moves the deny-log parsing out of the Computer tool into `lib/api/sandbox/egress_deny_log.ts`: `partitionDenyLogEntries` (allowlist denials for the agent, harness denials for logging, unrecognized lines verbatim) now also returns the deduped blocked domains, and `collectEgressDenials` wraps the read plus the harness-denial logging so both callers report them the same way. The Computer tool's `<network_proxy_logs>` output is unchanged.
2. When a function invocation fails, the invocation resource reads its sandbox's deny log and appends the blocked domains to the runner error: `Egress blocked for: api.stripe.com. To allow them, add them to the manifest's "domains" and republish, or call request_egress_domain.` The error `code` is untouched, so callers keep classifying it the same way.
3. The Frames v2 skill tells the agent that a blocked fetch reports the blocked domains in the function error.

The read happens only on the failure path: it is a root exec round-trip kept off the fast-function happy path, and a function that swallowed a blocked fetch has already decided what its caller sees. The deny log is sandbox-global with a consumed offset, so under concurrent invocations in one Frame sandbox the domains are "blocked since the last read" rather than strictly this run's; the existing Computer tool has the same property.

## Tests

- `egress_deny_log.test.ts`: partitioning (allowlist rendering plus deduped domains, harness denials hidden but kept, unrecognized lines verbatim) and the hint wording for Frame and Pod owners.
- Invocation resource: a failed Frame invocation carries the blocked domain in its error; a successful one never reads the deny log; a deny-log read failure leaves the runner error untouched.
- Computer tool suite passes unchanged (its deny-log tests exercise the moved code through the bash tool).
- Biome and typecheck clean.

## Risk

Adds one root exec to the failure path of function invocations, bounded by the existing 2 s deny-log timeout and never fatal. Error messages get longer when domains were blocked; codes are unchanged. Worst case, a hint names a domain blocked by a concurrent invocation in the same sandbox. Safe to rollback.

## Deploy Plan

- [ ] Deploy `front`

body.title: Frames v2: declare egress domains in the manifest and file them as Pod or workspace requests on publish

labels.name: documentation-ack
labels.description: Used to acknowledge that documentation is up-to-date with this PR

body.body:
## Description

Frames v2 functions run in a Frame-owned sandbox whose egress is the workspace policy plus the Pod's when the Frame lives in a Pod. Nothing told an admin what a published function needs: the v2 publish is `dsbx frame publish <manifest>` with no other input, so unlike the legacy Pod Functions `publish` tool (which took a `domains` argument) there was no way to file egress requests. On-the-fly approvals don't help either: they write to the conversation's own policy, which function sandboxes never see.

Stacked on the `frames_v2` gate swap (`31909`).

**What this PR does:**

1. Adds a `domains` array to the Frames v2 manifest: exact domains or `*.example.com` wildcards, normalized and deduped, capped at the same 50 as a scope's pending-request section (constant now shared from `types/sandbox/egress_policy`). Persisted in the publication descriptor; old descriptors default to `[]`. `dsbx frame validate` surfaces malformed entries before publish.
2. After a successful v2 publish, files those domains as requests on the scope the Frame's sandbox inherits from (`FrameSandboxAdapter.resolveScope`, now public): the Pod, else the workspace. Never the Frame's own policy file, which no admin surface lists. A request failure never fails the publish.
3. Batches the policy writes: one read of the scope (plus the workspace layer when filing on a Pod, so workspace-allowed domains aren't re-requested), one write, one proxy invalidation per publish, via new `requestOwnerPolicyDomains` / `requestWorkspacePolicyDomains`. The single-domain helpers delegate to the batch. The batch is rejected whole if it would exceed the cap.
4. The shared helper (`egress_domain_requests.ts`) backs both Frame publish paths (fresh and legacy-replacement) plus `request_egress_domain` and the admin egress route. (An earlier revision also wired it into the Pod Functions publish tool; Pod Functions were removed on main in `31933` while this PR was open.) One behavior note for the existing single-domain surfaces: a domain the workspace already allows now reports `already_allowed` instead of filing a redundant Pod request.
5. `egressDomains` on the publish response (`filed` with requested / already-allowed lists, or `failed` with the reason) and on the CLI response struct so the agent sees what is pending. Frames v2 skill text updated: declare domains in the manifest, relay pending approvals to the user, `request_egress_domain` for domains discovered after publish.

The edit-text republish path deliberately does not re-file: the manifest is unchanged, so its domains were already requested.

> [!NOTE]
> The CLI prints `egressDomains` only once the sandbox image carries the rebuilt `dsbx`. Requests are filed server-side regardless; until then the agent just doesn't see the summary.

## Tests

- Manifest parsing: defaults, normalization and dedup, malformed domains, cap.
- Policy batch: classification with a single write, workspace-layer skip when filing on a Pod, no-write when nothing is new, cap rejection, malformed batch.
- Shared helper: Pod and workspace filing, failed batch, formatter wording.
- Publish: workspace scope, Pod scope honoring the workspace allowlist, already-allowed, at-cap failure with message, no domains declared.
- Biome and typecheck clean on `front` and `front-api`.

## Risk

Additive manifest field, additive response field, additive descriptor field with a default. Publish never fails on a domain request error. Worst case, a request lands on the wrong scope and an admin dismisses it, or the agent forgets to declare a domain and the function's fetch is denied at runtime as it is today. Safe to rollback.

## Deploy Plan

- [ ] Deploy `front` and `front-api`
- [ ] Rebuild the sandbox image with the new `dsbx` (agents see `egressDomains` from then on)
